Anatomy of a link

FIG. 01 · WHY THE KEY NEVER REACHES A SERVER
cashdrop.app/app/ Origin The only part any server receives.
#/claim? Fragment Browsers never transmit anything after the #.
d=7HqK2vR9… Ciphertext Seed, amount and note under AES-256-GCM.
&n=Yk3pQ1… Nonce 96 random bits, fresh every time.
&k=Zt8vW2… or &l=1 Key or a lock Add a password and the key leaves the link entirely.
How it works

Three moves for the sender. One for the recipient.

01

Seal

Amount, note, optional password. A fresh shielded address is derived on your device.

02

Fund

Send the amount plus a 0.0001 reserve from any shielded wallet. Save the recovery file.

03

Share

Paste the link into an encrypted chat. The password, if any, travels another way.

→ RECIPIENT

Claim

Open it, make a wallet if needed, and the browser proves and sweeps the funds locally.

FOR MERCHANTS

Take payment.
Keep no customer file.

Checkout turns any phone into a shielded point of sale. Plans sell subscriptions where the customer approves every renewal. To confirm a payment, your browser rebuilds the merchant wallet from its recovery file and scans testnet itself. No account, no dashboard, no customer record.

CashDrop?
Why Zcash

The chain learns less.

On a transparent chain, a payment link would publish who paid whom, how much, and everything they do next. Zcash’s shielded pool hides all of it, and CashDrop keeps both the funding and the claim shielded.

HONEST LIMITS

A link is cash.
Treat it like cash.

Shielding hides the payment from the chain. It can’t hide a link pasted into the wrong chat, so here is exactly where the edges are.

Read the full threat model →
  1. 01Whoever holds the complete unlocked link can claim first.
  2. 02A compromised device or insecure chat can leak it.
  3. 03The lightwallet gateway sees request timing and network metadata.
  4. 04Deadlines are reminders in this beta, not consensus timelocks.
  5. 05Testnet only. Independent security review comes before mainnet.
Under the hood

Two browsers and a blockchain.
Nothing in between.

NODE 01Sender browserWebZjs WASM wallet, fresh seed, AES-GCM envelope.
→ SHIELDED FUNDING TXOne-time addressLives in the Zcash shielded pool. Holds the funds, nothing else.
→ LINK, OFF-CHAINRecipient browserDecrypts locally, scans compact blocks, builds the proof.
→ SHIELDED CLAIM TXRecipient walletAny shielded testnet address, or one made on the spot.

A static PWA. No CashDrop API, user database, custodial wallet or analytics pipeline. There is nowhere for your keys to go.

Before you drop.

Is this real Zcash?

Yes. The beta runs on the public Zcash testnet with real shielded addresses and transactions. Testnet coins have no monetary value.

Does the link contain the money?

It carries encrypted recovery material for a fresh shielded wallet. Treat it like cash: whoever unlocks the complete link can claim first.

Can CashDrop recover my link?

No. It’s non-custodial. Save the recovery file when you create a drop, fund, checkout or plan.

Can a Plan charge me automatically?

Never. CashDrop holds no wallet authority. Every renewal is a payment the customer chooses to send.

Is it mainnet-ready?

Not yet. This release is testnet-only and needs an independent security review before it handles real value.
